MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 26, 2020

Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:02 p.m., on May 26, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on May 21, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project v.
  The City of Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  1  May 26, 2020
   Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Questioned the City Attorney and City Council on a lack of
  transparency regarding the voting system for the November election. She expressed concern
  that it is 160 days from the election and the City still does not have a legal election code.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel—Existing Litigation (Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d)
  of Section 54956.9) Name of case: Donaldson vs City of Mission Viejo.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update on both Closed Session
items. The Council provided direction to staff but no reportable action was taken.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that it is past time for Mission Viejo to open its Council Chamber to
the public. She said that the public podium is where people stand for what they believe is right.

DEPARTMENT HEAD UPDATES REGARDING COVID-19 ACTIVITIES

In lieu of individual Department Head updates, the City Manager shared a video that featured the
work and dedication of City employees during the COVID-19 pandemic.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 7 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 12, 2020, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated May 1, 2020 in the Amount of $210,972.69

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated May 8, 2020 in the Amount of $1,193,223.34

City Council Minutes  2  May 26, 2020
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  2019 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 20838)-Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation
  of the Notice of Completion.

5.  Alicia Parkway, Jeronimo Road, and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation
  (CIP 20837)

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer, and
  authorized staff to advertise for bids for the subject project.

6.  Contract Amendment for Janitorial Related Products at City Facilities

  Approved first amendment for Waxie Sanitary Supply for janitorial related products at city
  facilities for the period of July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020 in an amount not to exceed $12,000.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

7.  2020 Fourth of July Fireworks Spectacular

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum to approve
  the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee authorizing
  the annual Mission Viejo Fourth of July Fireworks Spectacular on Saturday, July 4, 2020.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

8.  Extension of the Proclamation of a Local Emergency for COVID-19

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Mayor Goodell, to extend the
  existing Proclamation of a Local Emergency Due to COVID-19 through June 9, 2020.

City Council Minutes  3  May 26, 2020
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

9.  Resolution Authorizing Execution and Delivery of a Municipal Equipment Lease
  Agreement, Approving Related Documents and Actions and Review of Proposed Cart
  Fee Rates

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg announced that this item will be continued to a future date.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

10. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

11. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

12. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum stated that she is ready to come back to the Council Chamber for either
the first or second meeting in June, as long as safety measures are in place for staff and the public.
She commended staff on the filming and editing of the Virtual Memorial Day ceremony and joked
that someone said that the Council should have been wearing masks. Due to the excellent editing,
it looked like they were all in the studio filming together. She noted that she also loved the drive
through memorial banners in the Library parking lot. Council Member Bucknum shared that she
fostered a high energy dog named Spencer from the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center. She
thanked the Animals Services Department for finding foster homes for animals until they can be
placed in their forever homes. Lastly, she said she hoped that everyone had a great Memorial Day
weekend.

City Council Minutes  4  May 26, 2020
 Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths echoed Council Member Bucknum regarding the Virtual Memorial Day
Ceremony and he thanked staff for their efforts. He also thanked staff for getting the word out so
quickly regarding the re-opening of City businesses as the State moves to Stage 2. In conclusion,
Council Member Raths complimented the City’s Chamber of Commerce and noted that they are
excited to get back to business.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs agreed that the Council Chamber should be opened as soon as possible,
whether it’s the first or second meeting of June. He gave kudos to City staff for the extraordinary
editing of the Virtual Memorial Day event. He also informed the public that item 9 was removed
from the agenda in order to receive more than just one bid for the leasing of golf carts at Casta del
Sol Golf Course. Council Member Sachs noted that he spoke with the manager of Mission Viejo
Country Club who has been a tremendous help in getting the City bids from the top three golf cart
manufacturers. The bid coming in from Yamaha Golf Carts, which is the Rolls Royce of golf carts,
is an extraordinary deal and he thanked the Manager of the Country Club for going above and
beyond with his help. Council Member Sachs said that he was angered by a news report that equated
those that gave their life in service to this Country to those that have died of the COVID-19 virus.
He shared a quote from Ronald Reagan from a past Memorial Day Service: “Our young men and
women in the military that have given their lives have given two lives. One, the life that they have
led to this point, but they have also given up a life that they could have led by not sacrificing for
this Country.” Council Member Sachs stated that he finds it abhorrent for people to compare a
soldiers’ ultimate sacrifice with COVID-19. Both are sad but Memorial Day is about those that
stepped in front of danger not those who caught a cold. He said he doesn’t mean to demean the
virus but they are two very different things.

13. Consideration of Establishing a Minimum Threshold for City Council Mileage
  Reimbursement and Managing Toll Road Use

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that this proposal is an insult while families and businesses are
  struggling and it also appears to be more evidence of grandstanding.

  Council Member Sachs presented his report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to adopt a
  minimum threshold of 15 miles per trip for reimbursement and no toll road charge
  reimbursement.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, indicated that she attends many events throughout the City and that
  the miles per trip add up. She also asked if this could be an option for the Council Members
  to waiver reimbursement if they so desire.

  Council Member Bucknum and Mayor Goodell agreed that the toll road reimbursement should
  remain and Council should have the option to cross off those amounts for which they don’t
  want reimbursement.

City Council Minutes  5  May 26, 2020
   Council Member Sachs amended his motion as follows:

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to adopt a
  minimum threshold of 15 miles per trip for reimbursement.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  Bucknum, Goodell, and Kelley
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked staff for the Virtual Memorial Day Ceremony and stated it was so
well done. She said she enjoyed hearing from the guest speakers - Colonel Griffith who is the
Commanding Officer of the City’s Adopted Marina Battalion, as well as U.S Army Colonel John
Bly who is Commanding Officer for the Recruiting Battalion for Southern California. Mayor Pro
Tem Kelley commented city staff for going above and beyond during the COVID-19 shut down.
She encouraged the public to watch the video that was shown earlier on the City’s YouTube
channel. She also commended Mayor Goodell for his weekly videos to keep the public informed of
what is going on throughout the City. She outlined her attendance at a drive by congratulation
parade for English and Drama Teacher of the Year, Kim Siplivy at Newhart Middle School. She
said it was a very moving to see students driving by waving and presenting flowers and School
Board Member Judy Bullockus was there to present a plaque to Ms. Siplivy. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
congratulated students graduating from 8th grade and especially high school seniors missing their
graduation ceremonies, proms and all the other senior events that occur this time of year. She
wished them good luck as they go forward into the next phase of the lives. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem
Kelley announced that the next blood drive will be June 22 from noon to 6:00 p.m. in the Saddleback
Room at City Hall and she encouraged residents to donate blood due to the short supply at this time.
Appointments can be made RedCrossBlood.org.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell commended staff, Robert Schick, Karen Hamman, and Eric Winter for the excellent
work done on the Virtual Memorial Day Ceremony. He announced that tomorrow he will be
filming a piece on the opening guidelines for the community. He thanked Father Angelus from St.
Kilian Church for the wonderful job he did in the Memorial Day video with his thoughtful words
and invocation. Mayor Goodell noted that he spoke with Father Angelus earlier today and he
commended the City and staff for the excellent efforts they are doing during this time. Mayor
Goodell also thanked Colonel Griffith, Colonel Bly, the Color Guard from last year, Veterans of
Foreign Wars and the Sergeant that played the bugle. He said he is ready to come back to the
Council Chambers for the next meeting if staff has social distancing protocols in place as well as
other safety measures. Mayor Goodell announced that the City will be entering Stage 3 and as soon
as the Governor gives the green light and the City will be opening the Recreation Centers very soon.
He commended residents for doing their best in getting along to get through this and the COVID-
19 numbers and results prove this. Lastly, Mayor Goodell encouraged businesses to call County
Supervisor Lisa Bartlett to encourage her to release funds to the cities immediately.

City Council Minutes  6  May 26, 2020
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:49 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 9, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 9, 2020

City Council Minutes  7  May 26, 2020
